objective: Resolve what the 2026-10-23 field test left open about frozen-M7 parameter variants on the development cohort: (1) which low-payload variants keep an encode/decode CPU ratio near 1.0 when re-measured in SEPARATE paired runs (CPU noise across sessions, not more repeats inside one run), (2) whether the payload/CPU trade-off curve has a knee between batch 100 and 300 with the 32 KiB dictionary, (3) the 44 configurations never measured. Exact typed round trips; payload bytes only (no dictionary delivery or framing cost is measured here). Development-only evidence: nothing here is a confirmed discovery. Do not repeat a configuration without saying which uncertainty the repeat resolves.

research_program.objective: Quantify the payload/CPU trade-off against the frozen default with replicated, cross-session CPU evidence and cover the unmeasured region.

tracks.question: Which M7 variants dominate the default on payload bytes/event and codec CPU, and where is the knee of the trade-off?
Which near-CPU-neutral low-payload candidates keep their CPU ratio in separate paired sessions (cross-session noise)?
Do the 44 never-measured configurations contain anything not already dominated?

hypotheses.statement: The campaign knowledge store holds a verified view of what is measured and what is uncertain.
hypotheses.prediction: A free briefing task verifies the store and exposes frontier, uncertainty and unmeasured regions to the Director.

hypotheses.statement: The near-CPU-neutral low-payload candidates (for example 100/32/base/fixed) keep encode and decode CPU ratios within 3% of 1.0 across separate paired runs.
hypotheses.prediction: Re-measured in a later, separate run, the ratio stays inside 0.97..1.03 for both encode and decode; otherwise the earlier neutrality was within-session noise.
